findings.trigger_condition: The edge stream contains many distinct, unequal unhashable node values, for example [("n0", [0]), ("n1", [1]), ..., ("nN", [N])].
findings.root_cause: Every unhashable value is searched linearly through all previously registered unhashable values in _id_of, so registering N distinct unhashable nodes performs quadratic equality comparisons.
findings.impact: Large valid inputs can incur O(N^2) time and excessive resource use, violating the requirement to handle the dependency graph without an avoidable asymptotic scalability failure.
findings.suggested_validation: Generate 10,000 edges whose dependency values are distinct lists, such as [(i, [i]) for i in range(10000)], and measure registration time or equality-call count; expected near-linear behavior, while this implementation performs approximately 50 million prior-value comparisons.

confirmation.evidence: unhashable-deps probe: t(1500)=0.0478s, t(3000)=0.1847s, ratio 3.86x on 2x input => quadratic

findings.trigger_condition: Two distinct node objects compare equal, but one is hashable and the other is unhashable; for example, define an unhashable U whose __eq__ returns True for integer 1, then use edges [(U(), "d"), (1, "d")].
findings.root_cause: The identity registry uses separate lookup domains for hashable and unhashable values. The unhashable path compares only against unhashable_nodes, while the hashable path compares only within hash_buckets, so equality across those domains is never checked.
findings.impact: Equal-but-not-identical node values are treated as separate graph nodes, violating value-based deduplication and first-appearance semantics. The example should produce [["d"], [the first U instance]], but produces [["d"], [the U instance, 1]].
findings.suggested_validation: Use class U: __hash__ = None; __eq__ = lambda self, other: other == 1. Run dependency_layers([(U(), "d"), (1, "d")]); expected one dependent node because U() == 1, but actual output contains two dependent nodes.

confirmation.evidence: reproduced: 3 logical nodes for equal hashable/unhashable pair; matches supplemental check cross_hashability FAIL for phi_2 in replay-v2
